item.title: After Global Economy Shudders, Trump Zigzags on Whether War Is Nearing End
item.summary: The president told reporters at a news conference in Florida that the fighting is “going to be ended soon” but added that the U.S. would strike Iran harder if needed.

item.title: Fear and Hope for Iranians Trapped Between Bombs and Defiant Rulers
item.summary: Many in Iran feel helpless in the face of their entrenched system, and some are becoming increasingly embittered by the fierce American and Israeli bombardment.

item.title: Iran Choosing Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader Signals Defiance Amid War
item.summary: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei could prove to be even more radical than his father and predecessor, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed by the U.S. and Israel at the start of the war.

item.title: Ukraine Helps U.S. Bases in the Mideast With Stopping Drones
item.summary: As the war in Iran spreads, Kyiv is eagerly offering its hard-won expertise and advanced technology to counter Iranian drones.

item.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards: The Spine of a Militarized State
item.summary: With their pervasive military, political and economic clout, the Guards are often considered the main impediment to regime change, or any change, in Iran.

item.title: A Loose Band of Emerging Powers Is Divided Over Iran
item.summary: Brazil, China and Russia all denounced the U.S.-Israeli attacks, but other nations in the BRICS group haven’t, even though Iran is a fellow member.

item.title: Black Rain and Health Fears After Strikes on Iran Fuel Depots
item.summary: Health experts warn of long-term respiratory and neurological risks as smoke from burning oil spreads across the region.

item.title: Oil Falls and Stocks Rise After a Day of Drastic Swings
item.summary: The price of oil had spiked to nearly $120 a barrel on Monday, drawing remarks by President Trump that he believed the war on Iran was “very complete.”

item.title: On the Road With Zelensky, Weathered, Weary and Fighting On
item.summary: Ukraine’s leader, Volodymyr Zelensky, traveled east to visit frontline troops trying to stave off Russian attacks, and invited reporters for The New York Times to go with him.

item.title: New Supreme Leader Inherits Sprawling, Secretive Office That Dominates Iran
item.summary: His father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, had turned what was traditionally a religious affairs office into a shadowy national security juggernaut.
